vocabulary.meaning: containing substances that are good for health and growth
examples: The company tried to create a more nutritious pizza.
Vegetables can make a meal more nutritious.

vocabulary.meaning: a unit used to measure the energy provided by food
examples: The new recipe contains fewer calories.
People need different numbers of calories depending on activity levels.

vocabulary.meaning: a type of fat that can raise cholesterol when eaten in large amounts
examples: The pizza was designed to contain less saturated fat.
Many processed foods are high in saturated fat.

vocabulary.meaning: a substance used for flavour that contains sodium
examples: Too much salt can contribute to high blood pressure.
The recipe uses herbs to reduce the amount of salt.

vocabulary.meaning: an amount of food served to one person
examples: A smaller portion can reduce calorie intake.
The restaurant offers different portion sizes.

vocabulary.meaning: food placed on top of another food, especially pizza
examples: Vegetables are a popular pizza topping.
She chose mushrooms and peppers as toppings.

vocabulary.meaning: grain that keeps all parts of the seed and usually contains more fibre
examples: The pizza base was made with whole-grain flour.
Whole grains can be part of a balanced diet.

vocabulary.meaning: containing suitable amounts of different foods or nutrients
examples: The meal is more balanced when served with a salad.
A balanced diet includes a variety of food groups.

vocabulary.meaning: a set of instructions and ingredients for preparing food
examples: The chef changed the recipe to reduce fat.
This recipe uses less cheese than a traditional pizza.

vocabulary.meaning: a food or choice intended to be better for health than another option
examples: The restaurant markets the pizza as a healthy alternative.
Fruit can be a healthy alternative to a sugary dessert.
